status: Source implementation verified locally; not included in the published SDK/runtime 0.11.0 or deployed Worker.
change: Native WASI fexec dispatch resolves shebang scripts through the same bounded loader as path exec. Rust owns process-local regular-file aliases, descriptor rights, independent offsets and close-on-exec admission. Effect reads the original executable descriptor bytes and loads bounded interpreters; the descriptor buffer view avoids a second host-side byte copy.
cases: Real published sh reads the inherited /dev/fd/12 script, preserves arguments and environment, and commits its file effect.
Open script remains executable after its original pathname is renamed or unlinked.
Alias reads start at offset zero without changing the original offset of two.
Alias write, create and no-follow opens fail; rights cannot exceed those on the original descriptor; absent descriptor numbers return ENOENT.
CLOEXEC and explicit-close script descriptors fail ENOENT before replacement; the old frame and existing shared data offset and CLOEXEC flags survive.
Existing binary fexec, native path exec, start traps, signals, pending children and bounded interpreter behavior remain covered.
limits: Only regular-file, read-only descriptor aliases and followed metadata are supported; no devfs mount, directory or pipe alias support.
Direct libc cd/exec synchronization, other interpreter runtimes, PTY and remaining AgentOS parity gates stay open.
Production proof and archive distribution for this source increment remain pending. The published 0.11.0 artifacts are unchanged.
Native test timings do not establish production latency, throughput or cost.

verification.binaryCloseOnExec: Both CLOEXEC and explicit-close binary fexec cases pass, with the source descriptor absent in the replacement image. Script cases return ENOENT and preserve the original source descriptor and its flags.
